-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m6p1t2 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Instances, Blocks, MaxClock, Lease, MaxVer
NONE == "none"
VARIABLES rec, owner, deadline, snap, target, clock
vars == <<rec, owner, deadline, snap, target, clock>>

Valid(b) == owner[b] # NONE /\ clock <= deadline[b]

Init ==
    /\ rec = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> NONE]
    /\ deadline = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ target = [i \in Instances |-> NONE]
    /\ clock = 0

Acquire(i, b) ==
    /\ target[i] = NONE
    /\ (owner[b] = NONE \/ clock > deadline[b])
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = i]
    /\ deadline' = [deadline EXCEPT ![b] = clock + Lease]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = b]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = rec[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, clock>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ target[i] # NONE
    /\ LET b == target[i] IN
        /\ owner[b] = i
        /\ clock <= deadline[b]
        /\ snap[i] = rec[b]
        /\ rec[b] < MaxVer
        /\ rec' = [rec EXCEPT ![b] = rec[b] + 1]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
        /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadline, clock>>

Abort(i) ==
    /\ target[i] # NONE
    /\ LET b == target[i] IN
        /\ (owner[b] # i \/ clock > deadline[b])
        /\ owner' = IF owner[b] = i THEN [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NONE] ELSE owner
        /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, deadline, clock>>

Release(i) ==
    /\ target[i] # NONE
    /\ LET b == target[i] IN
        /\ owner[b] = i
        /\ clock <= deadline[b]
        /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
        /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![i] = NONE]
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, deadline, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, owner, deadline, snap, target>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, b \in Blocks : Acquire(i, b)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Abort(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Release(i)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleOverwrite ==
    \A i \in Instances : target[i] # NONE => snap[i] <= rec[target[i]]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {i1, i2}
    Blocks = {b1, b2}
    MaxClock = 3
    Lease = 2
    MaxVer = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleOverwrite
nl:
A subway signalling installation coordinates train movements over a small pool of track blocks. Two independent dispatch instances share the same pool of blocks, and each block carries a shared occupancy record that is stamped with a version number every time it is updated. Because the record is shared, a stale write from one instance must never silently overwrite a fresh write made by the other. To arbitrate access, an instance takes out a time-limited lease on a block before touching its record, and the lease automatically expires once the signalling clock passes its deadline. When an instance acquires a lease it snapshots the record's current version, and it is only permitted to commit an update if it still holds a valid, unexpired lease and its snapshot still matches the record. If another instance has meanwhile bumped the version, the snapshot is stale and the commit is refused, so the update cannot be lost. An instance may also abort and drop its work if it discovers its lease has lapsed. The clock ticks forward independently, causing outstanding leases to expire.
SAFETY PROPERTY: An instance working on a block never holds a snapshot version that exceeds the block's committed record version, so no stale write can overwrite a fresher one.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m6p2t4 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Workers, Lobbies, Population, MaxClock, Lease, MaxCap
NONE == "none"
VARIABLES pool, seated, cap, leaseOf, expiry, clock
vars == <<pool, seated, cap, leaseOf, expiry, clock>>

SumSeated ==
    LET f[S \in SUBSET Lobbies] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN seated[x] + f[S \ {x}]
    IN f[Lobbies]

Held(l) == leaseOf[l] # NONE /\ clock <= expiry[l]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Population
    /\ seated = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
    /\ cap = [l \in Lobbies |-> 1]
    /\ leaseOf = [l \in Lobbies |-> NONE]
    /\ expiry = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]
    /\ clock = 0

TakeLease(w, l) ==
    /\ (leaseOf[l] = NONE \/ clock > expiry[l])
    /\ leaseOf' = [leaseOf EXCEPT ![l] = w]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![l] = clock + Lease]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, cap, clock>>

Seat(w, l) ==
    /\ leaseOf[l] = w /\ clock <= expiry[l]
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ seated[l] < cap[l]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ seated' = [seated EXCEPT ![l] = seated[l] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, leaseOf, expiry, clock>>

Leave(l) ==
    /\ seated[l] > 0
    /\ seated' = [seated EXCEPT ![l] = seated[l] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, leaseOf, expiry, clock>>

Resize(l, c) ==
    /\ c \in 1 .. MaxCap
    /\ c >= seated[l]
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![l] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, leaseOf, expiry, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, seated, cap, leaseOf, expiry>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers, l \in Lobbies : TakeLease(w, l)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, l \in Lobbies : Seat(w, l)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Leave(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies, c \in 1 .. MaxCap : Resize(l, c)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

PopulationConserved == pool + SumSeated = Population
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    Lobbies = {l1, l2}
    Population = 3
    MaxClock = 3
    Lease = 2
    MaxCap = 2
INVARIANT PopulationConserved
nl:
A matchmaking service for a multiplayer game moves players between a shared waiting pool and a handful of game lobbies. Every player currently in the system is either idle in the waiting pool or seated in exactly one lobby, and the service must never create or lose a player while shuffling them around. To fill a lobby, a matchmaker worker first takes a short-lived lease on that lobby so two workers cannot fight over the same seats; the lease carries a deadline and lapses once the session clock passes it. While holding a valid lease a worker may seat one waiting player into the lobby, provided the lobby is below its current capacity, or a player may leave a lobby and return to the waiting pool. Lobby capacities are not fixed: an operator can resize a lobby up or down at runtime as demand changes, but resizing only adjusts the seat ceiling and never adds or removes players. The clock advances on its own, expiring stale leases so another worker can take over.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of waiting players plus the number of seated players across all lobbies always equals the fixed total population, so no player is ever created or destroyed.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m2p4t1 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Parts, Capacity, Weight
VARIABLES phase, vote, inflight, committed
vars == <<phase, vote, inflight, committed>>

BookVolume ==
    LET f[S \in SUBSET Parts] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN committed[x] + f[S \ {x}]
    IN f[Parts]

PledgeVolume ==
    LET g[S \in SUBSET Parts] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN
             (IF vote[x] = "yes" THEN Weight ELSE 0) + g[S \ {x}]
    IN g[Parts]

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ vote = [p \in Parts |-> "pending"]
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ committed = [p \in Parts |-> 0]

StartVoting ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ inflight' = { [kind |-> "prepare", to |-> p] : p \in Parts }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, committed>>

CastVote(p, v) ==
    /\ [kind |-> "prepare", to |-> p] \in inflight
    /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
    /\ inflight' = (inflight \ {[kind |-> "prepare", to |-> p]})
                    \cup {[kind |-> "reply", from |-> p, val |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, committed>>

DeliverVote(p, v) ==
    /\ [kind |-> "reply", from |-> p, val |-> v] \in inflight
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = v]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {[kind |-> "reply", from |-> p, val |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, committed>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A p \in Parts : vote[p] = "yes"
    /\ BookVolume + PledgeVolume <= Capacity
    /\ committed' = [p \in Parts |-> IF vote[p] = "yes" THEN Weight ELSE committed[p]]
    /\ phase' = "done"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, inflight>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ (\A p \in Parts : vote[p] # "pending")
    /\ ((\E p \in Parts : vote[p] = "no") \/ BookVolume + PledgeVolume > Capacity)
    /\ phase' = "done"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, inflight, committed>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase = "done"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ vote' = [p \in Parts |-> "pending"]
    /\ inflight' = {}
    /\ committed' = [p \in Parts |-> 0]

Next ==
    \/ StartVoting
    \/ \E p \in Parts, v \in {"yes", "no"} : CastVote(p, v)
    \/ \E p \in Parts, v \in {"yes", "no"} : DeliverVote(p, v)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BookWithinCapacity == BookVolume <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Parts = {p1, p2}
    Capacity = 3
    Weight = 2

INVARIANT BookWithinCapacity
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which several member firms submit indicative orders that must be committed together through a two-phase commit driven by a central coordinator. In the first phase the coordinator broadcasts a prepare request to every participant; each participant replies with a vote message. All of these messages travel over an asynchronous bus that may deliver them in any order, so prepare requests and votes can be reordered arbitrarily before they are processed. The shared order book has a strict volume ceiling that must never be breached no matter how the votes arrive. Once the coordinator has collected the votes, it commits the batch only if every participant voted yes and the combined volume of the yes votes still fits under the book's capacity; otherwise it aborts and the book is left untouched. A commit applies the whole batch atomically to the book, while an abort discards it. Because the capacity check gates the commit, the accumulated book volume can never exceed the ceiling.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The committed volume in the shared order book never exceeds the fixed capacity ceiling.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m9p6t3 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Machines, MaxEpoch, MaxStock
VARIABLES curEpoch, cached, actEpoch, stock
vars == <<curEpoch, cached, actEpoch, stock>>

Init ==
    /\ curEpoch = 0
    /\ cached = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ actEpoch = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> MaxStock]

Reconfigure ==
    /\ curEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ curEpoch' = curEpoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cached, actEpoch, stock>>

Sync(m) ==
    /\ cached[m] < curEpoch
    /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![m] = curEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, actEpoch, stock>>

Dispense(m) ==
    /\ cached[m] = curEpoch
    /\ stock[m] > 0
    /\ actEpoch' = [actEpoch EXCEPT ![m] = curEpoch]
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = stock[m] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, cached>>

Restock(m) ==
    /\ stock[m] < MaxStock
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = MaxStock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, cached, actEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Sync(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Dispense(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Restock(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthorizedEpochOnly ==
    \A m \in Machines : actEpoch[m] <= cached[m] /\ cached[m] <= curEpoch
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    MaxStock = 2
INVARIANT AuthorizedEpochOnly
nl:
A network of vending machines is coordinated by a central controller that occasionally reconfigures the fleet by advancing a global epoch number, for example when prices or product mappings change. Each machine caches the epoch it currently believes is in force. Whenever the controller reconfigures, it increments the global epoch, and individual machines only learn about the new epoch when they synchronise, which they may do lazily. A machine is allowed to be slow at synchronising but it never fails outright, so it can always eventually catch its cached epoch up to the current one. The critical rule is that a machine may only dispense a product while its cached epoch matches the current global epoch; a machine still running on an old, stale epoch is not authorised and must be refused. Every dispense a machine performs is stamped with the epoch under which it acted. A stale machine that has not yet synchronised therefore cannot perform an authorised action, and no dispense may ever be stamped with an epoch higher than the machine's own cached authorisation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No machine ever performs a dispense stamped with an epoch greater than its own cached epoch, and no cached epoch ever exceeds the current global epoch, so stale or unauthorised machines cannot act.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m1p6t4 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS N, MaxCap
Stations == 0 .. (N - 1)
Succ(s) == (s + 1) % N
VARIABLES token, active, spool, cap
vars == <<token, active, spool, cap>>

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ active = [s \in Stations |-> FALSE]
    /\ spool = 0
    /\ cap = 1

PassToken ==
    /\ ~active[token]
    /\ token' = Succ(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, spool, cap>>

StartPrint(s) ==
    /\ token = s
    /\ ~active[s]
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, spool, cap>>

FinishPrint(s) ==
    /\ active[s]
    /\ spool < cap
    /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ spool' = spool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap>>

ChangeCapacity(c) ==
    /\ c \in 1 .. MaxCap
    /\ c >= spool
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, active, spool>>

DrainSpool ==
    /\ spool > 0
    /\ spool' = spool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, active, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E s \in Stations : StartPrint(s)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : FinishPrint(s)
    \/ \E c \in 1 .. MaxCap : ChangeCapacity(c)
    \/ DrainSpool

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyTokenHolderActs == \A s \in Stations : active[s] => s = token
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    MaxCap = 2
INVARIANT OnlyTokenHolderActs
nl:
A print shop runs several print stations arranged in a logical ring, and a single control token circulates around that ring. The token is passed from each station to its successor, and only the station currently holding the token is authorised to begin a print job onto the shared spool. A station that does not hold the token is an unauthorised or stale participant and must never begin printing. When the token holder starts a job it becomes active, and it finishes by depositing the rendered job into the spool buffer before it can pass the token onward. The spool buffer has a capacity that operators can change at runtime, raising it when the shop is busy or lowering it for maintenance, and a finished job can only be deposited while the spool is below its current capacity; a separate courier drains completed jobs out of the spool. Because starting a print requires the token, at most the single authorised station is ever mid-print, and no station without the token can act.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A station is ever actively printing only if it currently holds the ring token, so no unauthorised station acts.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m5p2t0 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Ctrl, TotalLoad
VARIABLES served, shed, ballot, alive
vars == <<served, shed, ballot, alive>>

QuorumFor(d) == 2 * Cardinality({c \in Ctrl : alive[c] /\ ballot[c] = d}) > Cardinality(Ctrl)

Init ==
    /\ served = TotalLoad
    /\ shed = 0
    /\ ballot = [c \in Ctrl |-> "none"]
    /\ alive = [c \in Ctrl |-> TRUE]

CastVote(c, d) ==
    /\ alive[c]
    /\ d \in {"none", "shed", "restore"}
    /\ ballot[c] # d
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shed, alive>>

ExecuteShed ==
    /\ QuorumFor("shed")
    /\ served > 0
    /\ served' = served - 1
    /\ shed' = shed + 1
    /\ ballot' = [c \in Ctrl |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

ExecuteRestore ==
    /\ QuorumFor("restore")
    /\ shed > 0
    /\ shed' = shed - 1
    /\ served' = served + 1
    /\ ballot' = [c \in Ctrl |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED alive

Crash(c) ==
    /\ \A d \in Ctrl : alive[d]
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, shed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl, d \in {"none", "shed", "restore"} : CastVote(c, d)
    \/ ExecuteShed
    \/ ExecuteRestore
    \/ \E c \in Ctrl : Crash(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LoadConserved == served + shed = TotalLoad
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Ctrl = {c1, c2, c3}
    TotalLoad = 2
INVARIANT LoadConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed amount of electrical load that is at any moment either being served or deliberately shed. A cluster of controllers decides collectively whether to shed or restore load, and no shedding or restoration happens unless a quorum (a strict majority) of the controllers has voted for that action. Each controller casts a vote of shed, restore, or none, and may change its mind before a decision is executed. When a majority currently votes to shed and there is still served load, one unit of load is moved from the served pool into the shed pool; when a majority votes to restore and there is shed load, a unit moves back. Executing a decision clears the votes so the next round starts fresh. Crucially, the total amount of load is a conserved quantity: units only ever move between the served and shed pools, and none are created or destroyed. One controller may crash silently at any time, dropping out of voting without warning, but because decisions require a majority quorum the remaining controllers can still act.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The served load plus the shed load always equals the fixed total load, so no load unit is ever created or destroyed.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m0p1t3 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Clients, MaxVer, MaxInv
IDLE == "idle"
WORK == "working"
VARIABLES inv, ver, phase, base, applied
vars == <<inv, ver, phase, base, applied>>

Init ==
    /\ inv = 1
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ phase = [c \in Clients |-> IDLE]
    /\ base = [c \in Clients |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {}

BeginEdit(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = IDLE
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = WORK]
    /\ base' = [base EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inv, ver, applied>>

CommitSell(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = WORK
    /\ base[c] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ inv > 0
    /\ inv' = inv - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[client |-> c, at |-> ver]}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED base

CommitRestock(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = WORK
    /\ base[c] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ inv < MaxInv
    /\ inv' = inv + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[client |-> c, at |-> ver]}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED base

Retry(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = WORK
    /\ base[c] # ver
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inv, ver, base, applied>>

Abandon(c) ==
    /\ phase[c] = WORK
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![c] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inv, ver, base, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clients : BeginEdit(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : CommitSell(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : CommitRestock(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Retry(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Abandon(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A e1, e2 \in applied : (e1 # e2) => e1.at # e2.at
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Clients = {c1, c2}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxInv = 2
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a single central inventory record for a popular product, and several machine clients update that record concurrently using optimistic locking. The record carries a value and a version stamp. Before changing the record a client reads it and remembers the version it saw as the base of its edit; a client may be slow and sit on that snapshot for a while, but it never fails outright. When the client tries to commit its change, the commit succeeds only if the record's version still equals the base version it read; the successful commit applies the change and bumps the version. If another client has committed in the meantime, the version has moved on, the base is stale, and this client must retry from a fresh read rather than clobber the newer value. A client may also simply abandon its pending edit. Because every successful commit consumes exactly the version it was based on, two edits can never both commit against the same base version, which is precisely the situation that would cause a lost update.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two committed updates were ever based on the same record version, so no committed update is silently lost by being overwritten.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m6p4t3 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Processors, Banks, Ceiling, Amt, Lease, MaxClock
NONE == "none"
VARIABLES batchTotal, holder, expiry, pending, clock
vars == <<batchTotal, holder, expiry, pending, clock>>

LeaseValid(p) == holder = p /\ clock <= expiry

Init ==
    /\ batchTotal = 0
    /\ holder = NONE
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ pending = [b \in Banks |-> FALSE]
    /\ clock = 0

AcquireBatch(p) ==
    /\ (holder = NONE \/ clock > expiry)
    /\ holder' = p
    /\ expiry' = clock + Lease
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchTotal, pending, clock>>

Submit(b) ==
    /\ ~pending[b]
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchTotal, holder, expiry, clock>>

Post(p, b) ==
    /\ LeaseValid(p)
    /\ pending[b]
    /\ batchTotal + Amt <= Ceiling
    /\ batchTotal' = batchTotal + Amt
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, expiry, clock>>

CloseWindow(p) ==
    /\ LeaseValid(p)
    /\ batchTotal' = 0
    /\ holder' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expiry, pending, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchTotal, holder, expiry, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Processors : AcquireBatch(p)
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Submit(b)
    \/ \E p \in Processors, b \in Banks : Post(p, b)
    \/ \E p \in Processors : CloseWindow(p)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BatchWithinCeiling == batchTotal <= Ceiling
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Processors = {q1, q2}
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    Ceiling = 4
    Amt = 2
    Lease = 2
    MaxClock = 3
INVARIANT BatchWithinCeiling
nl:
A settlement agent runs interbank payments in batched windows, where each window has a strict liquidity ceiling that the total settled value must never exceed. Because several settlement processors could contend for a window, a processor must first take out a time-limited lease on the current batch before it may post anything into it; the lease expires once the settlement clock passes its deadline, letting another processor take over. Member banks submit payment instructions of a fixed value into a pending tray, and a bank may be slow to submit without ever failing, so its instruction simply waits until it is picked up. The processor holding a valid batch lease posts a pending instruction into the batch, but only if doing so keeps the batch total at or under the liquidity ceiling. The lease holder can also close the window, which zeroes the running total and releases the lease so a fresh window can begin. The settlement clock advances on its own, expiring stale leases.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The running settled total of the batch never exceeds the fixed liquidity ceiling.

EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Cars, MaxEpoch, MaxServe
VARIABLES curEpoch, token, enrolled, crashed, serving
vars == <<curEpoch, token, enrolled, crashed, serving>>

    /\ curEpoch = 0
    /\ token = [e \in Cars |-> FALSE]
    /\ enrolled = [e \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = [e \in Cars |-> FALSE]
    /\ serving = 0

Reconfigure ==
    /\ curEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ curEpoch' = curEpoch + 1
    /\ token' = [e \in Cars |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, crashed, serving>>

Enroll(e) ==
    /\ ~crashed[e]

    /\ curEpoch = 0
    /\ wardEpoch = [w \in Wards |-> 0]

    /\ wardEpoch[w] = curEpoch
    /\ stock[Central] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![Central] = stock[Central] - 1, ![w] = stock[w] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, wardEpoch, crashed>>

Return(w) ==
    /\ ~crashed[w]
    /\ wardEpoch[w] = curEpoch
    /\ stock[w] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![w] = stock[w] - 1, ![Central] = stock[Central] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, wardEpoch, crashed>>

CentralReclaim(w) ==
    /\ stock[w] > 0
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![w] = stock[w] - 1, ![Central] = stock[Central] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curEpoch, wardEpoch, crashed>>

Crash(w) ==
    /\ \A x \in Wards : ~crashed[x]

    \/ \E w \in Wards : SyncWard(w)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : Deliver(w)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : Return(w)
    \/ \E w \in Wards : CentralReclaim(w)

    Wards = {w1, w2}

    MaxEpoch = 3

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker manages a fixed number of blood units distributed across a central store and several ward fridges. Every unit lives in exactly one location at any moment, so the total number of units is a conserved quantity that must never change as stock is moved around. A central coordinator occasionally reconfigures the distribution plan by advancing a global epoch, and each ward caches the epoch it last learned. A ward may synchronise to catch its cached epoch up to the current one, possibly lazily. A ward is only authorised to move stock -- delivering a unit from the central store to itself, or returning a unit from itself back to the central store -- while its cached epoch matches the current global epoch, so a ward running on a stale plan cannot move stock. One ward may crash silently at any time and stop participating, but the units already sitting in its fridge are never lost and can still be reclaimed one at a time back to the central store by a central-side recovery step. Because every move only relocates a single unit between two real locations, the grand total of blood units is invariant regardless of reconfiguration or crashes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of blood units across the central store and all ward fridges always equals the fixed total, so no unit is ever created or destroyed.

nl:
A stock exchange opening auction is settled by a coordinator running successive commit rounds with the member firms, each round identified by a monotonically increasing round number. A round proceeds as a two-phase commit: the coordinator opens a round, collects each firm's vote, then closes the round. Firms can be slow: a firm caches which round it believes is current and may lag behind, but it never fails outright and can always catch up by synchronising its cached round to the coordinator's current round. The essential authorization rule is that a firm may only cast a vote for the round the coordinator is actually running: a slow firm still stuck on a previous, stale round is not authorized and its vote must be refused until it synchronises. Every recorded vote is stamped with the round in which it was cast, and opening a fresh round clears the previous round's votes. Consequently, at any moment, every vote currently on record was cast by a firm acting in the current round, and no stale or unauthorized firm can have a vote standing.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every recorded vote is stamped with the coordinator's current round number, so no stale firm from an earlier round ever has a standing vote.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p3t0 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Students, Courses, SeatsPerCourse
NONE == "none"
Seats == { [course |-> c, id |-> i] : c \in Courses, i \in 1 .. SeatsPerCourse }
CourseOf(s) == s.course
VARIABLES courseLock, seatLock, held, crashed
vars == <<courseLock, seatLock, held, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ courseLock = [c \in Courses |-> NONE]
    /\ seatLock = [s \in Seats |-> NONE]
    /\ held = [st \in Students |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = [st \in Students |-> FALSE]

AcquireCoarse(st, c) ==
    /\ ~crashed[st]
    /\ courseLock[c] = NONE
    /\ courseLock' = [courseLock EXCEPT ![c] = st]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seatLock, held, crashed>>

AcquireFine(st, s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[st]
    /\ courseLock[CourseOf(s)] = st
    /\ seatLock[s] = NONE
    /\ seatLock' = [seatLock EXCEPT ![s] = st]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<courseLock, held, crashed>>

Allocate(st, s) ==
    /\ ~crashed[st]
    /\ seatLock[s] = st
    /\ courseLock[CourseOf(s)] = st
    /\ s \notin held[st]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![st] = held[st] \union {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<courseLock, seatLock, crashed>>

ReleaseCoarse(st, c) ==
    /\ courseLock[c] = st
    /\ courseLock' = [courseLock EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seatLock, held, crashed>>

Crash(st) ==
    /\ \A x \in Students : ~crashed[x]
    /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![st] = TRUE]
    /\ courseLock' = [c \in Courses |-> IF courseLock[c] = st THEN NONE ELSE courseLock[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seatLock, held>>

Next ==
    \/ \E st \in Students, c \in Courses : AcquireCoarse(st, c)
    \/ \E st \in Students, s \in Seats : AcquireFine(st, s)
    \/ \E st \in Students, s \in Seats : Allocate(st, s)
    \/ \E st \in Students, c \in Courses : ReleaseCoarse(st, c)
    \/ \E st \in Students : Crash(st)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A a, b \in Students : (a # b) => (held[a] \intersect held[b] = {})
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system lets students claim individual seats in courses using two levels of locking. To register, a student process must first take a coarse lock on the whole course, and only then may it take a fine lock on a specific open seat within that course; this coarse-then-fine discipline prevents the lock ordering that would otherwise cause trouble. Once a student holds both the coarse lock on the course and the fine lock on a particular seat, it allocates that seat to itself, and the seat's fine lock is retained permanently as a record of ownership so the seat can never be locked or handed out again. A student releases its coarse lock when done so other students can work in the course. One student process may crash silently at any time; a crash quietly abandons any coarse lock the student was holding, but seats it has already been allocated stay allocated to it. The key guarantee is that no seat is ever allocated to two different students, because a seat's fine lock can be held by only one student and is never released after allocation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct students ever hold an allocation of the same seat, so no seat is double-allocated.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m4p1t2 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Controllers, Jobs, Cap
NONE == "none"
VARIABLES enqueued, queue, consumed, owner
vars == <<enqueued, queue, consumed, owner>>

Init ==
    /\ enqueued = {}
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ consumed = {}
    /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NONE]

Enqueue(i, j) ==
    /\ j \notin enqueued
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < Cap
    /\ enqueued' = enqueued \union {j}
    /\ queue' = queue \union {j}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED consumed

Consume(j) ==
    /\ j \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {j}
    /\ consumed' = consumed \union {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enqueued, owner>>

Recycle(j) ==
    /\ j \in consumed
    /\ consumed' = consumed \ {j}
    /\ enqueued' = enqueued \ {j}
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Handoff(i, j) ==
    /\ j \in queue
    /\ owner[j] # i
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enqueued, queue, consumed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Controllers, j \in Jobs : Enqueue(i, j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Consume(j)
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Recycle(j)
    \/ \E i \in Controllers, j \in Jobs : Handoff(i, j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostJob ==
    /\ enqueued = queue \union consumed
    /\ queue \intersect consumed = {}
=============================================================================
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line feeds cars through a single bounded work queue that two independent conveyor controllers share. Each car is a distinct job drawn from a shared pool, and either controller may enqueue a job. The queue applies backpressure: a controller may only enqueue a job while the queue holds fewer than its fixed capacity, so a full queue blocks further enqueues rather than dropping work. The queue is a shared record, and the danger being guarded against is a lost update -- an enqueue that updates one part of the shared record but silently fails to register the job in the queue, so the job vanishes. To make this checkable, the system tracks every job ever enqueued, every job still in the queue, and every job already consumed downstream, and it insists that these stay perfectly reconciled: every enqueued job is either still queued or already consumed, and no job is both at once. A downstream washer consumes jobs from the queue, and a consumed job may later be recycled back into the pool for a fresh wash. Because both controllers draw from the one shared pool, ownership of a queued job may also be handed from one controller to the other.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of all jobs ever enqueued always equals the disjoint union of the jobs currently queued and the jobs already consumed, so no enqueued job is ever lost.

vars == <<votes, budget, sealed, owner>>

Quorum(c) == 2 * Cardinality(votes[c]) > Cardinality(Controllers)

    /\ budget = [c \in Cars |-> 1]
    /\ sealed = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]

Withdraw(v, c) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, sealed, owner>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, budget, sealed>>

    /\ owner[c] = n
    /\ ~sealed[c]
    /\ budget[c] > 0
    /\ Quorum(c)
    /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ budget' = [budget EXCEPT ![c] = budget[c] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, owner>>

Recycle(c) ==
    /\ sealed[c]
    /\ sealed' = [sealed EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ budget' = [budget EXCEPT ![c] = 1]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]

    \/ \E v \in Controllers, c \in Cars : Withdraw(v, c)

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line runs two independent line instances that both draw cars from one shared pool. For each car, the irreversible final step is sealing on the protective wax coat, which can be applied at most once per car: once a car is sealed it is done and cannot be sealed again. Sealing is a safety-critical action, so it requires quorum approval: a strict majority of the line's inspection controllers must currently be voting to seal that car. Controllers cast votes to seal a car and may withdraw those votes if they change their mind before the seal happens. Because the two line instances share the pool, an instance must first claim an unowned car before it may seal it, and only the claiming instance performs the seal. Each car carries a single one-shot seal budget that starts at one and is consumed by sealing; a car that has been sealed has had its budget fully consumed. After a car is sealed and rolls off, it may be recycled back into the pool as a fresh, unsealed car with its budget and votes reset.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every sealed car has had its one-shot seal budget fully consumed to zero, so the irreversible seal is applied at most once per car.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m5p1t1 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Routers, Pids, MaxVer
VARIABLES recVer, proposals, ballots, applied
vars == <<recVer, proposals, ballots, applied>>

OpenPids == { p.pid : p \in proposals }
BallotsFor(pid) == { b \in ballots : b.pid = pid }
Quorum(pid) == 2 * Cardinality(BallotsFor(pid)) > Cardinality(Routers)

Init ==
    /\ recVer = 0
    /\ proposals = {}
    /\ ballots = {}
    /\ applied = {}

Propose(pid) ==
    /\ recVer < MaxVer
    /\ pid \notin OpenPids
    /\ proposals' = proposals \union {[pid |-> pid, base |-> recVer]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVer, ballots, applied>>

CastBallot(r, pid) ==
    /\ pid \in OpenPids
    /\ [pid |-> pid, voter |-> r] \notin ballots
    /\ ballots' = ballots \union {[pid |-> pid, voter |-> r]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVer, proposals, applied>>

Commit(pid) ==
    /\ \E p \in proposals : p.pid = pid /\ p.base = recVer
    /\ recVer < MaxVer
    /\ Quorum(pid)
    /\ recVer' = recVer + 1
    /\ applied' = applied \union {pid}
    /\ proposals' = { p \in proposals : p.pid # pid }
    /\ ballots' = { b \in ballots : b.pid # pid }

Discard(pid) ==
    /\ \E p \in proposals : p.pid = pid /\ (p.base # recVer \/ recVer >= MaxVer)
    /\ proposals' = { p \in proposals : p.pid # pid }
    /\ ballots' = { b \in ballots : b.pid # pid }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVer, applied>>

Rollover ==
    /\ recVer >= MaxVer
    /\ recVer' = 0
    /\ proposals' = {}
    /\ ballots' = {}
    /\ applied' = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E pid \in Pids : Propose(pid)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, pid \in Pids : CastBallot(r, pid)
    \/ \E pid \in Pids : Commit(pid)
    \/ \E pid \in Pids : Discard(pid)
    \/ Rollover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BaseNeverAhead == \A p \in proposals : p.base <= recVer
=============================================================================
nl:
An airport baggage router maintains a shared routing record that carries a version number, and updates to that record must be agreed by quorum. A router proposes an update by opening a proposal that snapshots the record's current version as its base. The inspection routers then cast ballots for open proposals; ballots travel over an asynchronous bus and may arrive in any order. A proposal may be committed only when a strict majority of routers have balloted for it and its base version still equals the record's current version, meaning nothing has changed underneath it. Committing bumps the record's version and clears the proposal and its ballots. If some other proposal has committed first, a proposal's base is now behind the record, so it is stale and must be discarded and re-proposed rather than applied on top of the newer state, which is exactly how a lost update is avoided. When the version reaches its ceiling the record rolls over to start a fresh cycle. At every moment a proposal's snapshotted base version can never run ahead of the record's actual version.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No open proposal ever holds a base version greater than the shared record's current version, so no proposal can commit on top of a version it never saw and silently lose an update.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m0p4t5 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Workers, Cap, MaxVer
IDLE == "idle"
WORK == "working"
VARIABLES occ, ver, snap, phase
vars == <<occ, ver, snap, phase>>

Init ==
    /\ occ = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ snap = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [w \in Workers |-> IDLE]

Read(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = IDLE
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = ver]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = WORK]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver>>

CommitAdmit(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = WORK
    /\ snap[w] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ occ < Cap
    /\ occ' = occ + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Retry(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = WORK
    /\ snap[w] # ver
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = IDLE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, ver, snap>>

AdminAdmit ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ occ < Cap
    /\ occ' = occ + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, phase>>

Depart ==
    /\ occ > 0
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ occ' = occ - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, phase>>

Rollover ==
    /\ ver >= MaxVer
    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, snap, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Read(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : CommitAdmit(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
    \/ AdminAdmit
    \/ Depart
    \/ Rollover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OccWithinCapacity == occ <= Cap
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    Cap = 2
    MaxVer = 3
INVARIANT OccWithinCapacity
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars into a wash zone that has a fixed bay capacity which must never be exceeded. Several intake workers admit cars concurrently using optimistic locking over a shared occupancy record that carries an occupancy count and a version stamp. A worker first reads the record, remembering the version it saw, then tries to commit an admit: the admit succeeds only if the version is unchanged since it read and the zone is still below capacity, in which case the occupancy rises by one and the version is bumped. If another worker admitted or a car departed in the meantime, the remembered version is stale and the worker must retry from a fresh read rather than admit on top of changed state. A privileged shift administrator holds an override: the administrator may admit a car directly without the optimistic version check, but even the override still refuses to admit once the zone is at capacity. Cars also depart, freeing a bay and bumping the version, and when the version stamp reaches its ceiling the record rolls the version back to restart the numbering.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The wash zone occupancy never exceeds the fixed bay capacity, whether a car is admitted by an optimistic worker or by the administrator override.

-------------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m1p6t2 --------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Nodes, PoolSize, MaxGen
Other(n) == CHOOSE m \in Nodes : m # n
VARIABLES holder, gen, authGen, pool, bin
vars == <<holder, gen, authGen, pool, bin>>

Init ==
    /\ holder = CHOOSE n \in Nodes : TRUE
    /\ gen = 1
    /\ authGen = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ pool = PoolSize
    /\ bin = 0

PassToken ==
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ holder' = Other(holder)
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authGen, pool, bin>>

Register(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ authGen[n] < gen
    /\ authGen' = [authGen EXCEPT ![n] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, pool, bin>>

Withdraw(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ authGen[n] = gen
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ bin' = bin + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, authGen>>

Restock ==
    /\ bin > 0
    /\ bin' = bin - 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, authGen>>

Reset ==
    /\ gen >= MaxGen
    /\ gen' = 1
    /\ authGen' = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, pool, bin>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Register(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Withdraw(n)
    \/ Restock
    \/ Reset

NoStaleAuthorization ==
    \A n \in Nodes : authGen[n] <= gen /\ (authGen[n] = gen => holder = n)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {g1, g2}
    PoolSize = 2
    MaxGen = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleAuthorization
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker is run by two independent tracker instances that share one pool of blood units. Exclusive access to the pool is arbitrated by a single control token that circulates between the two instances in a ring. Each time the token is passed, a fresh token generation number is minted, so the previous holder's authorization immediately goes stale. To actually act, the instance currently holding the token must first register its authorization at the current generation; only then, while it both holds the token and is registered at the current generation, may it withdraw a unit from the shared pool. An instance that still believes it is authorized under an older generation is stale and must not act, and an instance that is not the token holder is unauthorized and must not act either. A restock step returns dispensed units to the pool. When the generation counter reaches its ceiling, the tracker resets the generation numbering and clears all standing authorizations so nothing stale carries over. The design guarantees that whenever an instance is registered at the current generation, it is in fact the current token holder.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any instance registered at the current token generation is the current token holder, so no stale or unauthorized instance is ever authorized to touch the shared pool.
